title: Fix streaming keepalive timeouts causing partial degradation + add comms runbook references
author: Amara Diallo
release_notes: Reduces SSE/streaming disconnects on long-running generations by improving keepalive behavior and timeout handling; adds runbook references to guide customer-facing incident comms for streaming-only degradations.
body: Context: Over the last few weeks we’ve seen a recurring partial-degradation pattern where non-streaming requests are healthy but streaming (SSE) responses drop mid-generation with client-visible timeouts/disconnects. This shows up as elevated `stream_disconnect` and a spike in client retries, but overall 5xx for the API stays low (hence customers see “API degraded” while the issue is streaming-only). Support ticket SUP-18421 and multiple incident threads point to keepalive/idle timeout interactions on certain proxies/load balancers. Root cause: Our SSE keepalive implementation did not consistently reset the upstream idle timer because (1) keepalive frames were being buffered (flush not guaranteed) and (2) the server read/write deadlines were not updated when we emitted a keepalive comment, so long-running responses could hit `WriteTimeout` despite periodic keepalives. Under moderate load, batching can also delay first-byte enough that some clients interpret the connection as stalled even though generation is progressing. Changes in this PR: (1) Make keepalive emission “flush-safe” for SSE by forcing a flush after comment frames and ensuring we don’t coalesce keepalive writes with token payload writes. (2) Refresh connection deadlines on keepalive writes so the server-side write timeout doesn’t fire while a response is actively kept alive. (3) Add a small jitter to keepalive interval to avoid synchronized bursts across many connections (helps reduce periodic CPU spikes on the gateway). (4) Add explicit metrics/logging for keepalive-driven deadline refresh and disconnect reason bucketing to improve future incident classification. (5) Add runbook references in the gateway runbook and incident annotations so oncall can quickly choose the correct public component (Streaming) and use consistent customer guidance (retry/backoff, switch to non-streaming temporarily, consider fallback model/region). Safety/rollout: This is behind `STREAMING_KEEPALIVE_V2` (default on in us-east canary only). We will expand to us-west/eu-west after 24h if disconnect rate stays below baseline. If anything regresses, disable the flag and we revert to prior behavior. Customer-facing impact: Fewer unexpected streaming disconnects/timeouts for long-running generations; clearer operator guidance so we can report “Streaming degraded” instead of generic “API degraded” when applicable. Notes for status page comms: When this failure mode occurs, mark component(s) = Streaming (and region-specific Serving if isolated) and include workaround: retry with exponential backoff; for latency-sensitive flows consider temporarily disabling streaming; if pinned to a model family, try a compatible fallback model/version. See runbook links added below.
commits: gateway/streaming: flush keepalive frames + refresh write deadlines
gateway/streaming: add keepalive interval jitter + config defaults
obs: add disconnect reason bucketing + keepalive metrics
runbooks: link streaming-only degradation scenario + status component guidance
tests: add SSE keepalive deadline regression coverage
review_conversation: Rafael Mendes: Can we confirm this fixes the observed pattern where we see disconnects at ~55–65s even with keepalive enabled? Also please add a metric so we can alert specifically on keepalive timeout vs client cancel.

Amara Diallo (author): Yes — reproduced locally with the same proxy idle timeout settings; the disconnects were server-side `WriteTimeout` + buffered keepalive. Added reason bucketing (`server_write_timeout`, `proxy_idle`, `client_cancel`) and a counter `streaming_keepalive_deadline_refresh_total`.
Tomáš Novák: Please add a runbook snippet for status page component selection. We keep marking API degraded when only streaming is affected, which triggers a lot of support noise.

Amara Diallo (author): Added references to `runbook-status-page-update-procedure` plus a short “Streaming-only symptoms” section (elevated disconnects, non-streaming healthy) and recommended customer guidance.
Aisha Bello: Any risk of additional CPU from flushing too frequently? We should ensure keepalive interval defaults don’t increase write amplification.

Amara Diallo (author): Keepalive default stays at 15s; flush is only for keepalive frames (comments) and already the expectation for SSE correctness. Added jitter to prevent synchronized bursts; no change to per-token flush behavior.
Christine Wong: Small nit: in the runbook, use the customer-facing component name “Streaming” (not “SSE”) and avoid mentioning specific load balancer types.
Amara Diallo (author): Updated wording to “Streaming (server-sent events)” once, then just “Streaming”; removed provider-specific references.
incident_reference: Related to recurring oncall pattern discussed in #incidents and customer report SUP-18421 (streaming-only timeouts).
notes: Follow-ups: (1) After rollout, consider reducing first-byte latency for streaming by prioritizing initial token flush under high batch pressure (separate PR). (2) Evaluate adding region+route tags to streaming disconnect metrics for better component mapping (tracked in ENG-4827/ENG-4824 workstream).
